name: Arrays and Hashing
description: Use a hash map or set to count items or look them up in constant time.

name: Prefix Sums
description: Precompute running totals so range totals can be answered quickly.

name: Two Pointers
description: Move two indices through a sequence, often from both ends, to avoid checking every pair.

name: Sliding Window
description: Keep a contiguous range and grow or shrink it as you scan.

name: Stack
description: Use last-in, first-out order to track nested or unfinished items.

name: Monotonic Stack and Queue
description: Keep items in sorted order to find the next greater or smaller value, or a window's extreme.

name: Linked List
description: Rewire nodes in place, often with a dummy head or fast and slow pointers.

name: Binary Search
description: Halve a sorted range or a yes-or-no answer space on each step.

name: Sorting
description: Put items in a useful order first so the rest of the problem becomes simpler.

name: Intervals
description: Sort ranges by an endpoint, then merge them or check for overlaps.

name: Heap
description: Use a priority queue to get the current smallest or largest item repeatedly.

name: Tree Traversal
description: Visit nodes depth-first or level by level, combining results from children.

name: Binary Search Trees
description: Use the ordering of left and right subtrees to guide the search.

name: Trie
description: Store strings in a prefix tree to share common prefixes.

name: Backtracking and Brute Force
description: Try the possible choices, undoing each one and cutting off dead ends.

name: Graph Traversal
description: Explore connected nodes with BFS or DFS while tracking what has been visited.

name: Topological Sort
description: Order the nodes of a directed graph so dependencies come first.

name: Union-Find
description: Merge groups and check whether two items are in the same group.

name: Shortest Paths
description: Find minimum-cost routes through a weighted graph.

name: Minimum Spanning Tree
description: Connect all nodes at the lowest total edge cost.

name: 1-D Dynamic Programming
description: Build an answer from smaller answers along a single index.

name: 2-D Dynamic Programming
description: Build an answer from smaller answers over two indices, such as a grid or two strings.

name: Greedy
description: Make the locally best choice at each step, after checking that doing so is safe.

name: Bit Manipulation
description: Use binary operations on the bits of a number.

name: Math
description: Find a formula or numeric property that replaces simulating the process.

name: Strings
description: Process characters directly, for example by parsing or comparing.

name: Simulation and Implementation
description: Carry out the described process carefully, step by step.

name: Data Structure Design
description: Combine structures to support the required operations efficiently.

name: Number Theory
description: Use divisibility, primes, greatest common divisors, or modular arithmetic.

name: Chinese Remainder Theorem
description: Combine conditions on remainders for coprime or related moduli.

name: Combinatorics
description: Count arrangements with formulas rather than listing them.

name: Probability and Expected Value
description: Calculate chances or averages, often using linearity of expectation.

name: Game Theory
description: Reason about winning and losing positions under optimal play.

name: Geometry
description: Work with points, lines, and shapes, often using cross products.

name: Matrices and Matrix Exponentiation
description: Express a repeated transition as a matrix, then raise it to a power.

name: FFT and NTT
description: Multiply polynomials or compute convolutions faster than quadratic time.

name: Constructive Algorithms
description: Build any valid answer directly from a pattern you can prove works.

name: Divide and Conquer
description: Split the input, solve each part, and combine the results.

name: Meet in the Middle
description: Split the search space in half and combine the two lists of results.

name: Ternary Search
description: Narrow in on the peak or valley of a function with a single turning point.

name: Segment Tree and Fenwick Tree
description: Answer range queries and handle updates in logarithmic time.

name: Tree DP
description: Compute a value for each subtree from the values of its children.

name: Bitmask DP
description: Use a set of chosen items, stored as bits, as the dynamic programming state.

name: Lowest Common Ancestor and Tree Queries
description: Answer questions about paths between tree nodes after preprocessing.

name: String Hashing
description: Compare substrings quickly using rolling or polynomial hashes.

name: String Matching
description: Find occurrences of a pattern using prefix information, as in KMP or the Z-function.

name: Suffix Structures
description: Use suffix arrays or automata to answer questions about substrings.

name: Strongly Connected Components and Bridges
description: Find a graph's tightly linked groups or its critical connections.

name: Max Flow and Min Cut
description: Model limits as edge capacities and find the most that can pass through.

name: Bipartite Matching
description: Pair items from two groups so as many as possible are matched.

name: 2-SAT
description: Express either-or constraints as a graph on true and false choices.

name: Interactive Problems
description: Ask the judge questions and narrow down the answer within a query limit.

name: Expression Parsing
description: Evaluate or process nested expressions according to their structure.

name: JavaScript
description: Use closures, promises, and prototypes to build small utilities in JavaScript.
